papers.title: An Introduction to O-minimal Geometry
papers.abstract: These lecture notes on o-minimal geometry comprise six chapters: 1 - O minimal Structures. 2 - Cell Decomposition. 3 - Connected Components and Dimension. 4 - Definable Triangulation. 5 - Generic Fibers for Definable Families. 6 - Smoothness.

papers.title: Flexible algebraic curves and fake vanishing cycles
papers.abstract: We prove that complex curves in sufficiently ample linear systems on simply connected projective surfaces are topologically (spin) flexible: any (spin) mapping class of the underlying real surface extends to a topological mapping class of the ambient 4-manifold. As a corollary, we prove that smooth curves in the complex projective plane are topologically (spin) flexible. A consequence of topological flexibility is the existence of fake vanishing cycles, that is, simple closed curves on the underlying real surface that are not vanishing cycles, yet still bound a topologically embedded $(\pm1)$-framed disk in the surface exterior. We also give examples of pushed in Seifert surfaces in $D^4$ that are not topologically spin-flexible, but become spin-flexible after a single internal stabilization. Our methods utilize the equivariant intersection form on the surface exterior.

papers.title: Products and duality for framed 1-flow categories
papers.abstract: We describe a product between framed 1-flow categories and show that it satisfies the expected Cartan formula on its second Steenrod squares. We also describe a dual framed 1-flow category and show that, like the Spanier-Whitehead dual of spectra, the homology groups of a framed 1-flow category can be shown to be isomorphic to the cohomology groups of its dual and that this isomorphism can be shown to cooperate with the framed 1-flow category structure in a suitable sense.

papers.title: Contractible 4-Manifolds with Nonnegative Ricci Curvature and Euclidean Volume Growth
papers.abstract: We prove that every contractible smooth 4-manifold admitting a complete Riemannian metric with nonnegative Ricci curvature and Euclidean volume growth is homeomorphic to $\mathbb{R}^4$. More precisely, every compact subset lies in the interior of a connected compact regular domain with simply connected complement. The key construction produces compact domains whose boundaries admit positive scalar curvature and which are regular sublevels of global strictly three-convex Morse exhaustions. A topological criterion forces the exterior fundamental group to be trivial whenever it contains no nonabelian free subgroup and satisfies the resulting boundary, homological, and relative cell hypotheses; in the geometric application, this group is finite. Its proof uses a cellular formulation of the Gerstenhaber-Rothaus theorem and a smooth filling obstruction. The resulting complements give simple connectivity at infinity, and Freedman's recognition theorem completes the argument.

papers.title: Second homotopy modules and infinite homotopy stable classes of four-manifolds
papers.abstract: We construct infinitely many closed oriented smooth 4-manifolds which are all stably diffeomorphic but pairwise not homotopy equivalent. Our examples are distinguished by their second homotopy modules, and provide the first examples which demonstrate that stable diffeomorphism does not determine the second homotopy module. They have fundamental group $(\mathbb{Z}/4)^4*\mathbb{Z}$ and arise as doubles of presentation 2-complexes. In contrast, we give criteria for isomorphism of second homotopy modules of doubles of 2-complexes, covering finite abelian, quaternion, dihedral and symmetric fundamental groups. We also establish non-injectivity of the doubling construction by showing that there exist homotopically distinct presentation 2-complexes over $Q_{28}$ whose doubles are homotopy equivalent.

papers.title: Spectral Summation and Critical Asymptotics of Newton Knot Invariants
papers.abstract: The symmetric colored invariants of a knot are defined at integer colors, and Newton interpolation assembles them into a formal function of a continuous color variable. We sum it by $q$-Borel--Laplace summation and use the resulting analytic function to study the invariants as $q\to1$. For every knot and every rank, the critical summation level is a rational number determined by the growth of the colored invariants; when it is positive, the critical Borel transform is meromorphic in the whole plane. When the Newton coefficients have analytic tails, the Borel transform is assembled from convergent sums of simple poles along geometric progressions, and for such sums the Stokes jump of the Laplace sum determines every pole and residue. For an infinite family of twist knots containing the figure-eight knot, a positive Markov kernel gives an exact formula for the remainder of the Newton series. With it we show that, near a root of the Alexander polynomial, the rescaled analytic interpolation converges to Gaussian and Scorer-type profiles, uniformly for complex values of the rescaled color, and we determine how fast the rank may grow before these limits change. Finally, continuation in $\log q$ produces a logarithmic monodromy whose coefficient is a convergent pairing of the same Borel residues that give the Stokes jump. For the figure-eight knot, the asymptotics of this coefficient are governed by the hyperbolic volume at every rank.

papers.title: Linear programming certificates for dimension bounds of hyperbolic Coxeter polytopes
papers.abstract: We use linear programming to derive upper bounds for the dimension of hyperbolic Coxeter polytopes from local geometric and arithmetic estimates. Rational certificates give the bounds $57$ for finite-volume polytopes, $17$ for compact polytopes, and $15$ for compact arithmetic polytopes. In the finite-volume case, the certificate is a weight function on incidences between vertices and two-dimensional faces. In the compact cases, the inequalities concern squared norms of orthogonal projections of a fixed tangent vector at a vertex farthest from an interior point. We give a common formulation of these linear programs, prove monotonicity in the dimension threshold, and describe the exact verification of the certificates. The local estimates are taken from the companion geometric proofs.

papers.title: Alexander modules and Milnor fibers of topological line arrangements
papers.abstract: We study the Alexander module and a distinguished cyclic cover, which we call the \textit{topological Milnor fiber}, of the complements of topological line arrangements. For every topologically realizable combinatorial type with $n \geq 2$ lines, where $n$ is not a prime power, we prove that the first Betti numbers of its topological Milnor fibers are unbounded. Moreover, any finite abelian group occurs as a direct summand of the integral homology of a topological Milnor fiber within the given combinatorial type. As an application, we show that every topologically realizable combinatorial type with $n \geq 2$ lines admits a realization whose complement has no $2$-dimensional CW model.

papers.title: Cup products with volume classes in bounded cohomology
papers.abstract: Let $M$ be a complete Riemannian $n$-manifold, $n\geq 2$, and suppose that either $M$ is negatively curved, or that it is a locally symmetric space of non-compact type. Via integration over straight simplices, every top-degree bounded differential form $\omega\in \Omega_b^n(M)$ defines a bounded cohomology class in $H^n_b(M)$. We prove that every such class belongs to the annihilator of the cup product in the whole graded algebra $H^{\geq 1}_b(M)$. In the case of closed orientable surfaces, this generalizes a result of Marasco, and, via transfer, provides a new proof of the fact that the cup product of the bounded Euler class of $SL(2,\mathbb{R})$ with itself vanishes. Our result also applies to degree-3 bounded classes constructed by Soma and Farre, thus showing that, for surface groups and for free groups, the annihilator of the cup product is infinite dimensional also in degree 3.

papers.title: Freeness of crossed modules, augmented quandles, and augmented racks
papers.abstract: We study freeness of crossed modules, augmented quandles, and augmented racks. We show that the associated quandle functor and the associated crossed module functor are left adjoint to the natural forgetful functors. For a map $f\colon S\to G$, we define the free augmented rack $R_f\to G$ and the free augmented quandle $Q_f\to G$. If $C_f\to G$ denotes the free crossed module determined by $f$, then the associated crossed modules of $R_f\to G$ and $Q_f\to G$ are both isomorphic to $C_f\to G$. We also characterize free augmented quandles in terms of stabilizers. As applications, we prove that the canonical inner augmentation of every generalized Alexander quandle is free. For a classical knot quandle, the canonical inner augmentation is free if and only if the knot is a torus knot. For every $n$-knot with $n\geq2$, the canonical inner augmentation is also free.

papers.title: Fake surfaces for some potential Andrews-Curtis counterexamples
papers.abstract: Andrews and Curtis famously conjectured that every contractible $2$-complex $3$-deforms to a point and, in fact, it suffices to consider contractible closed fake surfaces. The traditional potential counterexamples are given as balanced presentations of the trivial group. In this article, we construct closed fake surfaces for the Akbulut-Kirby family of potential counterexamples using geodesic loops in a metric classifying space for the $3$-strand braid group. Concretely we construct a $(2n+1)$-vertex fake surface for $\mathrm{AK}_n$ with a cyclically symmetric $1$-skeleton. Our $7$-vertex fake surface for $\mathrm{AK}_3$ is the simplest fake surface whose Andrews-Curtis status is unknown.

papers.title: Determinant and quasi-alternateness of checkerboard colorable links
papers.abstract: We give a connected state expansion of the determinant of checkerboard colorable links and extend the notion of quasi-alternateness from classical links to this setting. We provide an obstruction to quasi-alternateness and we characterize classicality of alternating virtual links. Then, we show that quasi-alternateness is preserved under rational extensions of quasi-alternating crossings. Finally, we define the family of almost alternating virtual links. We show that extending the dealternator of an almost alternating virtual diagram of a quasi-alternating checkerboard colorable link preserves the quasi-alternateness.

papers.title: Combinatorial characterizations of the quantum $\mathfrak{sl}_3$ invariant of positive alternating links and 3-braids
papers.abstract: The $\mathfrak{sl}_3$ link polynomial is a higher rank relative of the Jones polynomial which can be studied entirely diagrammatically using Kuperberg's web calculus. Building on the work of Harper and Kalfagianni, we construct formulae for the fourth and fifth coefficients of the quantum $\mathfrak{sl}_3$ link invariant on positive alternating link diagrams in terms of data read from the associated Seifert graph. Then, we give a characterization of the invariant on positive alternating fibered links in terms of elementary symmetric polynomials. We also discuss behavior of our formulae under connected sums. We give formulations for the $\mathfrak{sl}_3$ invariant of even powers of the Garside element $\Delta_3\in B_3$ and a closed formula for the invariant on positive $3$-braids, resulting in a formula for the invariant on all $3$-braids.

papers.title: 10/8-inequality for a spin 4-orbifold with boundary and its application
papers.abstract: As an application of 10/8 inequality for a spin 4-orbifold with boundary, we give criteria of homology 3-spheres represented by certain framed links for having infinite order in the homology cobordism group of homology 3-spheres. Such a class of homology 3-spheres includes certain plumbed 3-manifolds, 1/odd surgeries along certain knots with many twists, for example, certain Montesinos knots, $(p,q)$ cable knots of any knot with some large $p$, $q$, etc.

papers.title: Fibered-knot braids and symplectic fake quadrics
papers.abstract: We construct aspherical symplectic four-manifolds with the rational cohomology ring of $S^2\times S^2$ by summing ruled surfaces along braided multisections. For each $m\geq1$, we form two symplectic sums with the same gluing map in the chosen surface markings and normal framings, using a stabilized braid for the trefoil in one sum and for the torus knot $T(2,7)$ in the other. Both sums have integral first homology $({\mathbb Z}/2)^2\oplus{\mathbb Z}/(4m)$. Their fundamental groups admit respectively $36$ and $24$ epimorphisms onto $S_3$, so the sums are nonhomeomorphic. We also vary the gluing while keeping the multisections fixed. In each of five product, twisted, and hybrid cases, this gives an infinite sequence in which the first homology groups have strictly increasing finite orders. All but finitely many members of each sequence admit no complex structure.

papers.title: One-Relator Products of Left-Orderable Groups
papers.abstract: We prove that, for left-orderable groups $A,B$ and a word $w\in A*B$ which is not conjugate into $A$ or $B$ and is not a proper power, the one-relator product $A*B/\left\langle\!\left\langle w \right\rangle\!\right\rangle$ is torsion-free, answering a question posed by Chen and Lodha. We do this by proving a relative asphericity result for the one-relator product. We also generalise the B. B. Newman Spelling Theorem to one-relator products and deduce that a one-relator product $A*B/\left\langle\!\left\langle w^k \right\rangle\!\right\rangle$ of left-orderable groups with torsion is hyperbolic relative to $\{A,B\}$.

papers.title: On the action of the mapping class group on the fundamental group of a surface
papers.abstract: We describe the action of the mapping class group $M(g,n)$ on the fundamental group of $S_{g,n}$, the complement of $n$ distinct points in a compact orientable surface of positive genus $g$. This is achieved by computing the image of the generators of $M(g,n)$ as outer automorphisms of the fundamental group.

papers.title: Seifert forms and slice Euler characteristic of links
papers.abstract: We define the Witt coindex $\beta$ of a rational bilinear form (not necessarily symmetric) as the codimension minus dimension of a maximal totally isotropic subspace. Levine gave a computable necessary and sufficient condition for $\beta=0$, but no algorithm of computation of $\beta$ had been known when $\beta>0$. Our main result is a computable necessary and sufficient condition for $\beta=1$ in the case when the symmetrized form is non-degenerate. As shown by Taylor, all upper bounds of the slice genera of knots based on their Seifert form can be derived from the Witt coindex of the Seifert form. The case of an odd $\beta$ does not apply to knots but we show that it provides an estimate of the slice Euler characteristic for the links with an even number of components. We illustrate our results with examples where the Witt coindex is used to show that a two-component link does not bound a locally flat cylinder in the four-ball, whereas any other known restriction does not show it.

papers.title: The Gilmer-Masbaum map is not injective on the Kauffman bracket skein module
papers.abstract: Gilmer and Masbaum use Witten-Reshetikhin-Turaev (WRT) invariants to define a map from the Kauffman bracket skein module to a set of complex-valued functions defined on roots of unity in order to provide a lower bound for its dimension. We compute the image of the evaluation map for a family of mapping tori of the 2-torus and find that the restriction of the map to certain homology classes is not injective. This provides an answer to a question posed by Gilmer and Masbaum in the latter paper. Moreover, we give a basis for the Kauffman bracket skein module in the case of the mapping torus of a power of the Dehn twist along the meridian of the 2-torus.

papers.title: State integrals for the quantized $\operatorname{SL}_2(\mathbb{C})$ Chern-Simons invariant
papers.abstract: Previous work of the author and N.\ Reshetikhin defines an invariant $\operatorname{Z}_{N}^{\psi}(K, \rho, \mu)$ of a knot $K$, a representation $\rho \colon \pi_{1}(S^{3} \setminus K) \to \operatorname{SL}_{2}(\mathbb{C})$, and a logarithm $\mu$ of a meridian eigenvalue of $\rho$. It can be interpreted as a geometric twist of the Kashaev invariant or as a quantization of the $\operatorname{SL}_{2}(\mathbb{C})$ Chern-Simons invariant and is defined via a discrete state-sum involving quantum dilogarithms. In this paper we show how to express $\operatorname{Z}_{N}^{\psi}(K, \rho, \mu)$ as a sum over contour integrals in a space parametrizing hyperbolic structures on the knot complement. Such state integral presentations are an important step in determining the asymptotics of quantum invariants as predicted by the Volume Conjecture. We discuss this perspective and the remaining obstacles to establishing exponential growth of $\operatorname{Z}_{N}^{\psi}$.

papers.title: Homological Topological Quantum Field Theories
papers.abstract: We develop a new framework for quantum invariants of $3$-manifolds by extending to cobordisms a homological construction of mapping class group representations. More specifically, we construct a $(2+1)$-dimensional topological quantum field theory (TQFT) that assigns to each surface the twisted homology of its unordered configuration space. The construction requires a choice of local systems on configuration spaces together with additional data. We formulate sufficient conditions on these data that guarantee the TQFT axioms, and we show that there are at least two useful examples satisfying them. One of them yields a homological construction of the projective Kerler--Lyubashenko TQFT, while the other recovers the Frohman--Nicas--Donaldson TQFT. In contrast to the classical algebraic constructions of quantum invariants, our approach is purely topological and relies on multi-trajectory spaces of cobordisms.

papers.title: Ending currents of hyperbolic group actions
papers.abstract: We develop a theory of ending currents for properly discontinuous isometric actions of hyperbolic groups on Gromov hyperbolic spaces, generalizing Thurston's ending laminations. Several natural generalizations are considered, which agree in the 3-dimensional hyperbolic setting but are otherwise distinct. We illustrate these invariants and their differences by several examples, including closed surface group actions on hyperbolic group extensions arising from Teichm\"uller theory and a geometrically finite action of a closed surface group on $\mathbb{H}^4$ with a single cusp that corresponds to a non-simple curve on the surface. We also discuss the conditions under which ending currents characterize geometrically finite actions, obtaining several equivalent conditions and some surprises, illustrated by an example of a geometrically infinite action whose ending currents are all supported on a single orbit of peripheral subgroups.

papers.title: Multivariable Alexander polynomials of twisted torus links via Dehn surgery
papers.abstract: Let $T(p,q;r,s)$ be the twisted torus link obtained from the torus link $T(p,q)$ by adding $s$ full twists to $r$ adjacent strands, and let $C$ be an unknotted circle encircling those strands. For all $p$, $q$, and $r$ we compute the multivariable Alexander polynomial of $T(p,q)\cup C$ in closed form. A relation of Silver and Williams between the Alexander polynomials of a link and of its $1/n$ Dehn fillings then gives a closed formula for the multivariable Alexander polynomial of every twisted torus link $T(p,q;r,s)$, answering a question of Adnan and Park. When $\gcd(p,q)=1$, so that $T(p,q;r,s)$ is a knot, the formula is a sum of $pr$ monomials with coefficient $+1$, divided by cyclotomic factors, and its exponents are governed by an elementary counting function on the orbit of $q$ modulo $p$. Because the numerator has no cancellation, we are able to give the degree for all $s$ and simple non-fiberedness and non-L-space criteria for infinite families of twisted torus knots.

papers.title: Positivity of minimal volume entropy for some closed manifolds with zero simplicial volume
papers.abstract: For every integer $m\ge4$, we construct a closed connected oriented smooth $m$-manifold whose simplicial volume is zero and whose minimal volume entropy is positive. This answers negatively the question, attributed to Gromov, whether vanishing simplicial volume implies vanishing minimal volume entropy. Each example has a connected regular five-sheeted covering with zero minimal volume entropy, so vanishing of this invariant does not descend through finite coverings.
